newsitem.title: UK: Conoco UK MacCulloch oilfield delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Conoco UK MacCulloch oilfield delayed again.

text.p: First oil from Conoco's MacCulloch field some 250 km north of Aberdeen in the central North Sea has been delayed for a fourth time and is unlikely to flow before July, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The start of production, originally due in December 1996, has been pushed back by weather-related delays but this time the problem is of a technical nature, they said.
"There is a problem with a riser from the seabed to the floating production vessel," said a source familiar with the project.

Conoco, operator of the field which has estimated recoverable reserves of 58 million barrels of crude oil, similar to North Sea benchmark Brent, said the start date had been put back from late May to June but could not be more specific.
"It's to do with the amount of commissioning work that still needs to be done," said a spokeswoman.
But industry sources said commissioning of the field would "certainly not" be completed next month.
Dupont unit Conoco holds 60 percent of MacCulloch's equity. LASMO North Sea Plc owns the remaining 40 percent.

Oil from MacCulloch will be transported to Britain's Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands but the field's floating production vessel, the North Sea Producer, will also be equipped to load shuttle tankers if pipeline capacity to Flotta is not available.
Production should peak at 50-60,000 barrels per day (bpd), maintaining that level for 15-18 months.
Surplus gas will be exported via the Frigg pipeline system to St.Fergus.
Two cargoes of Flotta crude belonging to Conoco and LASMO and originally scheduled to load in June were cancelled due to the delayed start-up of MacCulloch, oil traders said on Wednesday.
